question.text:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\textrm E[X] = \dfrac{11}{12},$ compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} 1 - x^2, & 0 < x < 1, \\[5pt] % this part integrates to 2/3 \dfrac{1}{6}, & 1 \leq x < 3,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

We compute $\textrm E[X^2],$ as follows:

\[\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= \int_0^3 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx + \int_1^3 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 x^2 \cdot (1-x^2) \, \textrm dx + \int_1^3 x^2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{6} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 (x^2- x^4) \, \textrm dx + \int_1^3 \dfrac{x^2}{6} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left. \left(\dfrac{x^3}{3}-\dfrac{x^5}{5}\right) \right|_0^1 + \left.\dfrac{x^3}{18}\right|_1^3 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{71}{45} \end{align*}\]

Therefore, the variance is given by

\[\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{71}{45} - \left(\dfrac{11}{12}\right)^2 \\[3pt] &\approx 0.74 \end{align*}\] rounded to $2$ decimal places.

question.text: Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$ \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x}{8}, \quad &0 \leq x \leq 4,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

First, we compute $\textrm E[X]{:}$

\[\begin{align*} \textrm E[X] &= \int_{0}^4 x \cdot \dfrac{x}{8}\, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^4 \dfrac{x^2}{8} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left. \dfrac{x^3}{24} \right|_{0}^4 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8}{3} \end{align*}\]

Then, we compute $\textrm E[X^2]{:}$

\[\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= \int_{0}^4 x^2 \cdot \dfrac{x}{8} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^4 \dfrac{x^3}{8}\, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left. \dfrac{x^4}{32} \right|_{0}^4 \\[5pt] &= 8 \end{align*}\]

Therefore, the variance is given by

\[\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &= 8 - \left(\dfrac{8}{3} \right)^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8}{9}. \end{align*}\]

question.text: The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\textrm E[X] = 0.65,$ compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places. \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{4}{5}, & 0 < x < 1, \\[5pt] % this part integrates to 4/5 \dfrac{1}{x^6}, & 1 \leq x,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

We compute $\textrm E[X^2],$ as follows:

\[\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= \int_0^\infty x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx + \int_1^\infty x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 x^2 \cdot \dfrac{4}{5} \, \textrm dx + \int_1^\infty x^2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{x^6} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 \dfrac{4x^2}{5} \, \textrm dx + \int_1^\infty \dfrac{1}{x^4} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left. \dfrac{4x^3}{15} \right|_0^1 + \left. \left(-\dfrac{1}{3x^3}\right) \right|_1^\infty \\[5pt] &= 0.6 \end{align*}\]

Therefore, the variance is given by

\[\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &= 0.6 - (0.65)^2 \\[3pt] &\approx 0.18 \end{align*}\] rounded to $2$ decimal places.

question.text: The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\textrm E[X] = e-1,$ compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$ \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{x}, \quad &1\leq x \leq e,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

We compute $\textrm E[X^2],$ as follows:

\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= \int_{1}^{e} x^2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{e} x \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left. \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right|_{1}^{e} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^2-1}{2} \end{align*}

Therefore, the variance is given by

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^2-1}{2} - \left(e-1 \right)^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4e-e^2-3}{2}. \end{align*}

question.text: The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\textrm E[X] = \dfrac{5}{3},$ compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$ \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x}{3}, & 0 < x < 2 \\[5pt] % this part integrates to 2/3 \dfrac{2(3-x)}{3}, \quad & 2 \leq x < 3 \\[5pt] 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

We compute $\textrm E[X^2],$ as follows:

\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= \int_0^3 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^2 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx + \int_2^3 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^2 x^2 \cdot \dfrac{x}{3} \, \textrm dx + \int_2^3 x^2 \cdot \dfrac{2(3-x)}{3}\, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^2 \dfrac{x^3}{3} \, \textrm dx + \int_2^3 \dfrac{6x^2-2x^3}{3} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left.\dfrac{x^{4}}{12} \right|_0^2 + \left(\dfrac{2x^3}{3} - \dfrac{x^4}{6}\right)\Bigg|_2^3 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 43 + \left( 18 - \dfrac{27}{2} \right) - \left( \dfrac{16}{3} - \dfrac{8}{3}\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4}{3} + \dfrac{11}{6}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{19}{6} \end{align*}

Therefore, the variance is given by

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{19}{6} - \left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right)^2 \\[3pt] &= \dfrac{7}{18}. \end{align*}
